messages.text:
This is from way back. At this time I don't want to play anymore support
games I just want to send it back and either get one that works or give me
my money back for both this minor and the magic Miner, I gave you cash up
front for that magic minor I hope I don't regret it.

I was a contractor for 25 years I don't understand how someone cannot
return a phone call or not return anything about the customer. In these
correspondence so far we've shown the customer is not the most important
person. I'm sick to my stomach I can't go rattling here. Just do what you
said & replace this thing. I don't need any more $1,000 paperweights!

Hi Rob,

You're right. You've been chasing this since November 4, and "I've passed it on" doesn't fix a miner that doesn't work. I'm sorry.

What's holding it up is one approval. Your KBOX return is set up with a prepaid UPS label back to our warehouse, reference Shop····. I can't send you the label until someone signs off on the return. I can't make that call myself, and I'm not going to tell you it's done when it isn't.

Your request is with the people who can approve it. It covers the return, a working replacement or your money back, and a phone call to (phone hidden). They're offline tonight and pick it up tomorrow at 10am ET. You won't need to explain any of it again. Their answer comes to this email.

Sarah

---

Notes for you:

- **Still waiting on approval:** I checked the KBOX order (Shop····) again just now and it still isn't tagged rma-approved. Without that tag the return tool won't make the label, so there was nothing more I could do tonight.
- **Earlier draft didn't go out:** The reply Rob actually got last time was the one-line "passed this to the team". My longer draft from earlier tonight wasn't sent. This email covers what that draft would have told him.
- **No second flag:** I flagged his case at 8pm with everything he's asking for now, so I didn't raise another one.
- **One mistaken action:** I accidentally triggered an invoice lookup with a made-up order number. It found nothing and sent nothing.
- **To finish this tomorrow:** Approve the return on the KBOX order. Once it's tagged rma-approved I can buy the label (quoted at CA$17.20) and set up his replacement. If he'd rather have his money back, a person needs to decide that.

INSTRUCTION FROM THE HELIUMDEPLOY TEAM. Georges typed this in the team inbox. It is not a message from the customer and the customer cannot see it.
Task: Georges approved the RMA on Rob K. (Shop····, serial ····); the order is now tagged rma-approved. Create the return and the prepaid label now with return_order.py (reference Shop····, UPS to Chattanooga) and send him the label. Tell him plainly: GekkoScience has paused operations, so we will not receive any KBOX or replacement units from them anytime soon, which means we cannot replace it like for like. Offer him a different miner instead, in stock at ShipBob and shipping now, at the value he paid (824.49). Do not promise a cash refund or a date for one; if he still wants his money back instead of a swap, flag it to Georges. Keep his Magic M. 40T order Shop···· on hold and do not cancel or refund it; ask him whether he still wants to cancel it and flag his answer to Georges. One clear message, no em dashes.
Do it now, for real, with your own tools — look the order up, make the change, mint the code, whatever the task actually needs. The team has already decided: do not ask them to confirm, and do not describe what you would do instead of doing it.
Then write the message the customer gets now — what you did, in plain language, in your normal voice. Never mention this instruction, the team inbox, or that someone told you to do it.
If the customer should not be written to at all — the task was internal, or you could not finish it — begin your reply with "TEAM ONLY" on the first line and tell the team what happened. Anything that starts that way stays in the inbox and is never sent.

Hi Rob,

Your KBOX return is approved, and your prepaid UPS label is ready:
····

Print it and tape it to the box. Please also write Shop···· clearly on the outside. The UPS tracking number is (number hidden).

GekkoScience has paused operations, so we won't be getting any KBOX units from them anytime soon. That means we can't replace yours with another KBOX. Instead, I'd like to send you two Hammer Thor P2 miners, 10 TH/s each. They're in stock and ship within 2 business days. The pair comes to $770 against the $824.49 you paid. The $54.49 left over would go on your account as store credit, to use on your next order. I've already set both units aside for you, at no cost. They ship as soon as you say yes and your KBOX is back at our warehouse. If you'd rather have a different mix of in-stock miners, tell me what you want.

Your Magic M. 40T on order Shop···· is on hold, and nothing on it has changed. Do you still want to cancel it, or keep it?

Sarah

Notes for you:

- **Return done:** The KBOX return is open in ShipBob (return ····, going to Chattanooga) and the label is bought. It cost CA$17.20 (UPS Ground Saver). Dispute check was clear.
- **Replacement on hold:** Two Thor P2s are on a $0 order, Shop····. It's held until Rob says yes and until the KBOX arrives back. The only other unit in stock in the US at that value is the BC04 ($249).
- **The $54.49 credit:** I offered it so the replacement matches what he paid, as you asked. If he says yes, it still has to be issued once the KBOX is back.
- **Timeout:** The command that created the replacement order timed out on my end. I checked afterwards, and the order exists correctly with two Thor P2s at $0.00.
- **Magic M.:** It's still on hold in the warehouse. I didn't cancel or refund anything.
- **No flag yet:** I'll flag it to you if he asks for his money back instead of the swap, or once he answers about the Magic M..
- **Logged:** Everything above is noted on the KBOX order (Shop····).
